The system shall support adding PDFs.
The system shall support reordering pages or whole files.
The system shall support removing items.
The system shall support rotating pages.
The system shall support splitting and merging PDFs.
The system shall support visually building a new output from selected sections.
The system shall provide simple page previewing so the user can verify what they are assembling before exporting.
The system shall never change the source files.
The system shall prompt before closing or discarding an unsaved layout to reduce the risk of accidental work loss.
The command-line scope should remain tentative for the moment.
The command-line interface is expected to be included in some form.
The first version may be trimmed if needed without blocking the release on a fully polished command-line interface.
The GUI should stay locked in now.
The GUI is the main experience.
Any changes shall be written only to a new output file or to a separate working copy inside the application's own workspace.
The system shall create a copied file only when it needs a temporary internal version to support the editing session.
If there are unsaved changes, the app shall prompt clearly before closing or discarding anything.
If multiple layouts are open, the app shall deal with each layout separately so the user knows exactly what will be lost.
The app shall distinguish between one layout with unsaved edits and several open workspaces.
The warning shall be specific rather than generic.
The app shall let the user save the open layouts that matter and discard only the ones they choose, if possible.
If a source item is missing or unreadable, the application shall prevent that item from being included in the final output.

If an item already added to an assembly later needs to be edited again, the assembly shall retain the reference to the source item or enough information to allow the user to replace or reselect it easily.
If a file was replaced with a different version, the system shall let the user point the assembly to the new file.
If a file was replaced with a different version, the system shall let the user verify that the pages or section still match what they expected.
The system shall make broken links obvious in the workspace so they do not get overlooked.
If the replacement version has different page counts or changed page order, the system shall warn the user before export.
If the replacement version has different page counts or changed page order, the system shall let the user adjust the selection before export.
The system shall perform the verification check inside the workspace.
The system shall let the user remap the affected pages in the workspace.
The application shall let the user choose exactly which pages repeat and how many times they repeat in the assembly.
When the same source is reused several times, the application shall keep those repetitions clear so the user can edit them independently.
The system should store enough metadata to detect when a source has moved, changed, or gone missing.
The app should make it clear which repeated instances are linked and which are already unique so there is no confusion.
The application shall keep the rest of the assembly usable so the user can continue working on unaffected parts.
